newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris may target businesses to plug deficit - Allegre.
newsitem.headline: Paris may target businesses to plug deficit - Allegre.

text.p: France's new Socialist-led government will impose a one-off charge on profitable businesses to raise cash if needed to curb the budget deficit, Education Minister Claude Allegre said on Thursday.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is to hold talks with his cabinet from 0930 GMT to review budget measures ahead of release on Monday of an audit of public finances that will show if France is on track to qualify for a single European currency.
"If necessary, it will be a question of one-off charges on companies which make big profits," Allegre told RMC radio.
"It's normal that those who make big profits in a difficult situation should contribute more than others. But there is no question of raising taxes," he said.
France needs to reduce its deficit towards a target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) to qualify for European economic and monetary union from 1999.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn has said any measures to curb the budget deficit -- expected by economists to be slightly above 3.5 percent -- could affect companies and well-off households, and involve budget savings.
But he has also said that any measures affecting companies would be set up to avoid dampening business investment.
